summary: A narrative piece following Mia Bennett, an employee managing anxiety at the marketing firm Donovan & Hughes, through a workday to show how the company's mental health policies have changed its culture. Introduced since September 5, 2023 after Daniel Jacobs' 2022 crisis, the measures include quiet rooms, in-house counselors, mandatory workshops, flexi-hours and peer groups. The piece stresses leadership, education and human connection in replacing stigma with support.
one_line: A day in the life of Mia Bennett shows how Donovan & Hughes' mental health policies and supportive culture help employees manage anxiety.
key_facts: Mia Bennett works at Donovan & Hughes, a marketing firm, and manages anxiety with medication, meditation and a careful morning routine; the story is set on October 17, 2023.
Since September 5, 2023, Donovan & Hughes has introduced new policies to support employee mental health.
The changes were prompted by Daniel Jacobs, a former manager who faced a mental health crisis in 2022.
Physical changes include 'quiet rooms', plants and ergonomic furniture.
Donovan & Hughes appointed in-house counselors for confidential appointments and made mental health awareness workshops mandatory for all staff.
The 'Wellness Champions' group of colleagues from various departments organizes 'walk and talk' sessions around the nearby park; members include Paul Thompson and Lydia Cheng.
A 'flexi-hours' policy lets Mia plan her day around when she feels most capable, including coming in earlier or working from home.
Jessica Reid from human resources and Marcus Li from accounting, who openly shares his journey with bipolar disorder, give Mia a sense of connection.
Dr. Helen Ramirez, a psychologist, is set to speak at the company on November 12, 2023 about navigating mental health in high-pressure environments.
CEO Richard Kaplan advocates mental health support, saying a happy workforce is an efficient one.
Under Kaplan, performance reviews now include considerations of mental health, so managers like Sandra Gomez can support team members individually.
Mia can now use the quiet rooms or request a brief pause without fearing rebuke, rather than masking her struggles as she used to.
